paper_metadata.title: Statistics-informed parameterized quantum circuit: towards practical quantum state preparation and learning via maximum entropy principle

experiments.description: Maximum Entropy Distribution Loader (MEDL) numerical validation for preparing single statistical distributions with known laws and parameters: chi-squared, exponential, normal (Gaussian), and Rayleigh.

algorithm.ansatz: fixed-structure SI-PQC with sparse-state-preparation-pair and QSVT-based imaginary-time evolution

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Distribution p(x) is encoded on n = ceil(log2 N) qubits; constraint functions fk(x) are loaded via unitary dilation and combined linearly with LCU; imaginary-time evolution is approximated by QSVT.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare |p> = sum_x (1/N) exp(sum_k lambda_k f_k(x)) |x> for a target statistical distribution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraints are encoded as conserved observables; no penalty terms. LCU combines constraints and QSVT implements exponentiation.

problem_instance.description: Preparation of four representative distributions with perfect prior knowledge of both distribution law and parameters.

dataset_specification.description: Discretized distributions on equally spaced points x_j; specific parameter sets shown in Fig. 2 for chi-squared, exponential, normal, and Rayleigh families.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretization on equally spaced points; normalization of constraint vectors; no empirical dataset preprocessing.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of experimental state probabilities against theoretical discretizations; error reported as vertical distance between scatter and line plots.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare measured amplitudes with theoretical discretized distributions; compute approximation error.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: general QSP / model-based precomputation / variational PQC / QGAN-style loading
speedup_claims.conditions: when prior statistical symmetries are available and M ≪ n
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is asymptotic and depends on model structure; success probability depends on filling rate F.

experiments.description: Weighted Distribution Mixer (WDM) numerical validation for preparing a four-component Gaussian mixture with partial prior knowledge of the distribution family and uncertain parameters/weights.

algorithm.ansatz: SI-PQC with digital-encoded latent space, analog-encoded latent space, and modified state-preparation-pair

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Latent parameters θ are encoded in a digital register of nθ = log Nθ qubits and converted to an analog-encoded latent space; visible data x is encoded on nx qubits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare sum_{θ,x} sqrt(P_para(θ) P_data(x; θ)) |θ>|x> for a parametric mixture distribution.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No penalty terms; mixture weights are represented by latent-space amplitudes and the MEDL state-preparation pair is replaced by a latent-space-controlled construction.

problem_instance.description: Preparation of a 4-mixture of normal distributions.

dataset_specification.description: Gaussian mixture with four components; parameters given in Fig. 4(b).

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretization of the target mixture distribution; no empirical preprocessing.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of experimental and theoretical discretized distributions.

experiments.description: Variational learning experiment for a Gaussian mixture model using SI-PQC, learning means, variances, and weights from data.

algorithm.variant: SI-PQC-based variational learning of Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical model parameters (means, variances, weights) are encoded into circuit rotation angles; the distribution family is assumed known.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize 1 - F(ρ(θ), ρ_data) over θ = {μ_k, σ_k^2, w_k}.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Maximum entropy principle with moment constraints; no penalty terms.

problem_instance.description: Learning a two-Gaussian mixture from data; target mixture shown in Fig. 6(a).

dataset_specification.description: Two-component Gaussian mixture with means 6 and 14, variances 16 and 22.5, weights 0.45 and 0.55.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Not specified beyond using the target distribution as observed data.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Track convergence of estimated means and variances over epochs; evaluate KL divergence and fidelity.

quantum_resources.num_variational_params: Parameters for means, variances, and weights; exact count not explicitly reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Initialization of variational parameters; extraction of means and variances from circuit angles during training.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelity and KL divergence; compare learned parameters to target values.

speedup_claims.factor: improved generalization, trainability, scalability, and interpretability due to only M independent gates
speedup_claims.baseline_method: general variational quantum machine learning models with O(kn) parameterized gates
speedup_claims.conditions: when the distribution family is known and only parameters/weights are learned
speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit numerical baseline accuracy or runtime is reported in the text excerpt.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not explicitly quantified for the learning experiment; general SI-PQC learning uses only M independent gates and O(log(1/(ϵF))) repetitions per gate.

experiments.description: Quantum-enhanced online risk analysis / Value-at-Risk estimation on empirical time-series data using SI-PQC and QMCI.

algorithm.variant: SI-PQC-based quantum Monte Carlo integration with quantum amplitude estimation for VaR
algorithm.ansatz: SI-PQC state preparation for empirical distributions

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Empirical asset-price distribution is encoded as a quantum state over n qubits; comparator and QAE are used to estimate tail probabilities for VaR.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR_α[X] = -inf_x {F(x) > α} via quantum estimation of P[X ≤ L] and binary search over L.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Conservative constraints derived from slowly varying observables; maximum entropy principle used to fit empirical distribution.

problem_instance.description: Online risk analysis of a one-dimensional Maxwell-Boltzmann time series with changing parameter a over time.

dataset_specification.description: Generated over 33000 timestamps from P(x)=sqrt(2/pi) x^2/a^3 exp(-x^2/(2a^2)); a varies across 11 segments of 3000 ticks each.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Sliding window of length 1000; incremental updates of E[X], E[X2], and E[ln X] from new ticks; first 1000 ticks shown for initialization.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare quantum VaR estimates at timestamps grouped by 100 against exact empirical VaR benchmarks for α = 0.95, 0.85, 0.05.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Incremental update of monitored expectations over a sliding window; update SI-PQC parameters from Eq. (14).
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Binary search over loss threshold after QAE-based tail-probability estimation to obtain VaR.

classical_baselines.unit: not numerically stated in text; shown as benchmark curves in figure

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical Monte Carlo / classical VaR estimation via numerical integration and binary search
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports quantum VaR curves matching empirical benchmarks, but does not provide explicit numerical error values in the text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: QMCI with SI-PQC: TTS = O(1) + 2^m t_Q (Poly3(n) + T_evaluate), with Poly3 in O(n log n); QAE query complexity N_repeat ~ 2^m
